_why_this_exists_before_the_review_does: AUT-PROP-006. This record is written as the seat's FIRST act, so a seat that dies leaves evidence that it looked rather than nothing at all. It is EMPTY and says so: publish_bar.clause_1_hardening_converged REFUSES any round with an open record at the commit it is grading, because an unfinished look must never be counted as a clean one.
central_claim: At least two recruiting interventional trials on ClinicalTrials.gov admit extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma through molecular eligibility criteria (a FET fusion family; a translocation-associated soft-tissue-sarcoma cohort) while neither names the histology among its listed conditions, so a condition search on the diagnosis does not return them; and the obvious remedy, a keyword-matched reachability map, is worse than no map, because both trials adjudicated as REFUSING the disease would have passed a keyword screen.

blockers.summary: §2 states the transport defect's trigger as the registry ESCAPING comparison operators. The committed fetcher source, which the paper itself cites in §7 as the fix, records that exact account as a hypothesis that was tested and REFUTED: the registry emits LITERAL angle brackets.
blockers.evidence: Paper §2: 'The fetcher passed registry payloads through an HTML stripper, which deletes spans between angle brackets; the registry escapes comparison operators the same way, so eligibility text lost characters'. scripts/lit_fetch_urls.py at the pin, lines 218-228, says the opposite in terms: 'ClinicalTrials.gov emits LITERAL angle brackets inside free-text eligibility criteria — "PLT < 100,000/mcL", "prednisone > 10 mg daily"', followed by '⚠ SUPERSEDED, RETAINED: this comment first said the trigger was HTML-ESCAPED brackets (`<`/`>`). That was wrong and the synthetic written from it did not reproduce the defect — modules survived. The real record settles it: 0 literal `<` and 13 orphaned literal `>` remain in the damaged file, which is the stripper's own footprint.' Both data artifacts the paper rests on carry the same refuted wording (fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json transport_integrity.defect: 'ClinicalTrials.gov escapes angle brackets in free text as backslash-< and backslash->'; emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json transport_integrity.the_known_defect: 'ClinicalTrials.gov escapes angle brackets in free text'), so the paper is faithfully propagating an account the repository has already paid to correct. A methods reader who implements a guard against escaped brackets reproduces the bug — which is precisely what the code comment records happening ('the synthetic written from it did not reproduce the defect').
blockers.fix: Replace 'the registry escapes comparison operators the same way' with 'the registry writes comparison operators as literal `<` and `>` inside free-text criteria, which the stripper reads as tag delimiters'. The same correction is owed to transport_integrity.defect in fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json and transport_integrity.the_known_defect in emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json, or the paper should note that those two records carry the superseded account.

blockers.summary: §4.1 says one query ran on the one non-US registry that answered. The committed sweep records TWO queries there, and the second returned a record the artifact calls the most relevant one the sweep produced, which the paper never mentions.
blockers.evidence: Paper §4.1: 'the query that ran there was the parent term *chondrosarcoma*, and it returns two trials'. non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json, endpoints[0]: {'registry': 'ISRCTN (UK)', 'result': 'HTTP 200', 'read': true, 'queries': ['chondrosarcoma', 'sarcoma AND fusion']}. The second query is recorded under isrctn_what_it_holds.query_sarcoma_and_fusion with total_count 1 and ISRCTN52235823 ('Nanopore-based methylome classification ... for ultra-rapid tumour diagnostics in soft-tissue sarcomas'), annotated '⭐_note: A DIAGNOSTIC study rather than a treatment one, and it is the most relevant record the sweep returned'. The paper's definite singular therefore misstates the instrument, and it omits a returned record in a paper whose subject is what a registry search does and does not surface.
blockers.fix: Write 'two queries ran there — the parent term *chondrosarcoma*, which returns the two trials below, and *sarcoma AND fusion*, which returned one diagnostic study (ISRCTN52235823) and no treatment trial'. One clause; it strengthens rather than weakens §4.1.

blockers.summary: §7 Data availability names two URL manifests that do not exist at this commit, and closes the list on three when a fourth manifest holds the one screen §2 singles out as the exception that carried eligibility text.
blockers.evidence: Paper §7: 'The URL manifests behind the 2026-08-07 sweep are `research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-targets.json`, `-c3.json` and `-c4.json`'. The suffix elision resolves to emc-clinical-sweep-targets-c3.json / -c4.json; `git ls-tree 78d345d3 research/literature/` returns emc-clinical-sweep-c3.json and emc-clinical-sweep-c4.json — no file with the 'targets-' stem exists. Separately, fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json retrieval.runs lists FOUR runs, and the second (slug 'ct-reverify-frontier-2026-08-07') has targets_file 'research/manuscripts/modality-census/lit-targets-frontier-capability-2026-08-07.json' (present at the pin). That manifest is the sole home of ct_sarcoma_2026_new — the unfielded screen §2 relies on ('one sarcoma screen was unfielded and did carry it') and the only source of eligibility text for the third of the nine molecularly-defined records (NCT06988475, retrieved_from.payload = ct_sarcoma_2026_new). A referee following §7 cannot reach two of the three named files and is never pointed at the fourth.
blockers.fix: Name the four manifests by their real paths: research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-targets.json, research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c3.json, research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c4.json and research/manuscripts/modality-census/lit-targets-frontier-capability-2026-08-07.json.

p1s.summary: The abstract states the remedy flatly as 'the fix', while §6.1 shows the remedy is unavailable in the gene-family case and demonstrably costly. The abstract-only reader takes away a clean fix the body itself complicates.
p1s.evidence: Abstract: 'the fix is that trials whose eligibility is molecular should list the histologies that molecular criterion admits'. §6.1: 'Where it names a gene family it does not exist: enumerating every histology an EWSR1, FUS or TAF15 criterion admits is an editorial act, not a transcription. NCT07188532 shows the cost, listing *round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusion* while §4 adjudicates it as refusing this disease.' The adjudication artifact confirms both halves — NCT07188532 listed_conditions = ['Ewing Sarcoma', 'Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion'] and verdict '⛔ DOES NOT ADMIT'. Nothing in the abstract carries the qualification, and nothing reads the abstract against §6, so an edit to either drifts silently.
p1s.fix: Add the qualification to the abstract's 'Why it matters' in one clause: '...should list the histologies that molecular criterion admits — which is a transcription where the criterion names a class and an editorial act where it names a gene family'.

p2s.summary: §5 says centre type is 'not measured', but the committed admitting criterion for NCT06571734 — the very field §3 row 2 summarises — carries a centre-type requirement the paper never reports, and its omission points the reader the direction §4 calls worse than no map.
p2s.evidence: emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json, adjudications[0].the_admitting_criterion_verbatim: 'Patients must have histologically confirmed diagnosis of metastatic or unresectable translocation-associated soft tissue sarcoma (TAS). Pathology must have been reviewed at a National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) designated centre.' Paper §3 row 2 reports only the first sentence's substance; §5 says 'Site geography, referral route and centre type are separate barriers and are not measured' and then names two observed instances (paediatric centre / age 10; Canadian sites) while omitting this third, which is inside the criterion the paper quotes from. By §4's own harm model ('a map that sends a patient toward a trial that will refuse them is worse than no map at all') this is the costly direction.

p2s.summary: §5 tells an adult reader that one of the two admitting trials 'enrols from age 10' and omits the committed fact that it has no upper age limit, which is the half that matters to an adult with this disease.
p2s.evidence: fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, NCT05918640: 'minimum_age': '10 Years', 'maximum_age': null, sponsor 'Children's Hospital of Philadelphia'. Paper §5: 'one of the two admitting trials is run by a paediatric centre and enrols from age 10'. In a Limitations bullet about barriers, 'paediatric centre' plus 'from age 10' reads as a children's trial; the committed record says the registry posts no maximum age. Adding four words ('and posts no upper age limit') removes a 'do not look' reading the artifact does not support.

p2s.summary: Half of 'at least two' rests on a criterion read out of a payload known to be transport-damaged and never re-fetched, and §2 discloses that for the QUOTE without saying it also bounds the ADJUDICATION.
p2s.evidence: fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, NCT05918640: 'removal_markers_in_eligibility_text': 1, 'verbatim_sentence_is_transport_clean': true. §2 says the quoted criterion 'is the sentence the artifact records as transport-clean rather than a re-read one'. But the record's ADMITS reading is an inference over the whole eligibility text, one span of which the stripper deleted, and the paper's own §4 shows exactly this failure — NCT06094101 is fusion-framed in its title and restricted to three histologies in a criterion that only a clean per-trial read exposed. The 2026-08-09 residual note ('⚠_residual: Comparison operators inside laboratory-value criteria may still be damaged. That does not affect any adjudication below') covers only the four trials re-fetched that day, not NCT05918640.

p2s.summary: §4.1 makes an unbounded claim about the one non-US registry from two queries, while every US claim in the paper carries an explicit floor.
p2s.evidence: Paper §4.1: 'In the non-US registry read here the disease appears only as an exclusion'. The evidence base is non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json endpoints[0].queries = ['chondrosarcoma', 'sarcoma AND fusion'], totals 2 and 1 — three records. §5's floors bullet is scoped to the US screens ('Candidates entered the pool through keyword screens on titles, conditions and interventions, and the fusion screen came back at its page limit'), and no equivalent bound is offered for ISRCTN. The artifact makes the same unbounded claim ('The disease is not indexed as a subject anywhere in this registry'), so the paper inherits rather than introduces it.

p2s.summary: §2's methods table cannot reach its own total: the screens it names sum to fewer studies than the unique count it reports in the same cell.
p2s.evidence: Paper §2: 'fusion (400 studies, its page limit), basket (199) and sarcoma (526) screens, plus a term search on the driver gene; 1,159 unique studies indexed'. 400+199+526+5 = 1,130, and with any overlap fewer. fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, retrieval.unique_studies_indexed = 1159 is correct, but it counts instruments the row does not name — task_2_widened_search.instruments lists seven, including ct_sarcoma_2026_new, ct_ewsr1_term and the EMC condition searches. A reader doing the arithmetic finds the row inconsistent with itself.

p2s.summary: §3's fourth row answers a different question in the 'listed conditions' column, hiding what NCT04151342 actually lists.
p2s.evidence: The column header is 'listed conditions'; the NCT04151342 cell reads 'observational: it enrols the patient and does not treat them'. The committed list is ['Cancer', 'Malignancies Multiple', 'Malignant Solid Tumor', 'Cancer, Therapy-Related', 'Molecular Sequence Variation', 'Genetic Alteration', 'Gene Fusion', 'Receptor Tyrosine Kinase Gene Mutation'] (adjudication artifact) — which includes 'Gene Fusion', the fact the adjudication's own reading leans on ('the condition list names Gene Fusion explicitly').

p2s.summary: The seven DETERMINE arms' targets are all in the committed record and none is this disease's driver, which the paper's 'a question for the trial team' hedge leaves the reader to assume the other way.
p2s.evidence: fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json lists the arms as ALK (NCT05770037), TMB/MSI (NCT05770102), ROS1 (NCT05770544), HER2 (NCT05786716), BRAF (NCT05768178), MET (NCT06988475) and BRAF V600 (NCT07440290); NCT05722886.interventions enumerates the same seven agents. None is keyed to a FET fusion or to NR4A3. §3's 'whether this disease's fusion matches an open arm is a question for the trial team' is true and correctly hedged, but the reader is not told that no currently open arm is keyed to the driver.

p2s.summary: §4.1's closing sentence about NCT06239272 has a literal reading that is false, because 'it does not' attaches to what the search returns rather than to what the trial admits.
p2s.evidence: Paper §4.1: 'for a patient inside that age bound the diagnosis search does return this trial, and for a patient biopsied after 30 it does not.' A condition search does not filter on the searcher's age: NCT06239272 lists 'Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma' among 42 conditions (fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, emc_in_listed_conditions: true), so the search returns it for everyone. What fails for a patient biopsied after 30 is admission, not retrieval — which is the paper's own §1 distinction.

p2s.summary: §5's staleness bullet implies every status in the paper is dated, but neither ISRCTN record carries one, in the section that tells a reader a named trial excludes them.
p2s.evidence: §5: 'Statuses go stale. Every status here is as posted on the retrieval date...'. non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json records only id, title, names_this_histology and how_it_names_it for ISRCTN07742377 and ISRCTN60791336 — no recruitment status and no registration date — yet §4.1 discusses both in the present tense alongside recruiting US trials.

p2s.summary: The verbatim FET criterion is quoted as a truncated prefix with no ellipsis.
p2s.evidence: Paper §3: 'verbatim: *Patients must have a known FET fusion (fusion that contains EWSR1, FUS, or TAF15)*'. The committed sentence continues: '... as documented by next generation sequencing, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) or Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH).' (fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, NCT05918640.verbatim_eligibility_sentence). The omitted half is a documentation requirement a reader would want, and the word 'verbatim' invites the reader to treat the quote as complete.

objections_i_raised_and_the_paper_alread: 'Eligible but unfindable' asserts eligibility the paper cannot establish — answered three lines below the title by the standing banner ('Nothing here says any trial would accept any particular patient: eligibility is each trial team's decision after their own review, and a registry record is a summary of a protocol rather than the protocol') and again in §5 bullet 2.

The two trials might be findable by a free-text search on the disease name, so 'unfindable' overclaims — answered by §5 bullet 4, which states that the registry's free-text search reads fields beyond the conditions list, that no free-text search on the disease name was run, and that whether one would surface these two trials is untested.

Counting an observational registry cohort as a reachable 'trial' inflates the headline — answered by §3's paragraph that keeps the fourth row separate ('A reachability claim that quietly counts an observational cohort alongside interventional trials inflates itself') and by the abstract's restriction to 'recruiting interventional trials'.

n = 2 is too thin to carry the title — answered by 'so two is a floor', by §5's floors bullet naming the fusion screen's page-limit truncation, and by that bullet turning §4's finding on the paper's own numerator.

The 'translocation-associated soft tissue sarcoma' cohort may mean only the three histologies the sponsor listed — answered verbatim in §5 bullet 2, which names it as the question only the trial team can answer.

A 403 from a registry cannot support any claim about what that registry holds — answered in §5 bullet 3 ('A refusal says what an endpoint would answer, never what a registry contains') and by the abstract's separation of the two refusals from the TLS failure, which is stated as not separable from a fault of our own — a stricter reading than the artifact's own.

The paper implies no listing anywhere names this disease — pre-empted in §4.1 by NCT06239272, verified: 42 listed conditions including 'Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma', RECRUITING, maximum_age 30 Years, criterion '1-30 years at the time of the biopsy'.

The RECRUITING flags may be years stale — answered in §5 by naming NCT03767075 and its April 2024 verification, which the artifact confirms (status_verified_date 2024-04, last_update_post_date 2024-04-25).

The transport defect could have corrupted the criteria the adjudications turn on — answered in §2 for NCT05918640 specifically, and in the 2026-08-09 artifact's pre-read module assertion (4/4 modules present in all four payloads) for the four trials re-fetched that day.
notes: I could not find a reading on which the central claim fails. Every load-bearing number checks out against the committed record: the 400/199/526 screens and 1,159 unique studies (retrieval.unique_studies_indexed); NCT06571734's seven conditions on 2026-08-09 against ten in the 2026-08-07 fielded screen; enrolment 73 and 5,500; NCT05918640 phase 1/2, RECRUITING, min age 10, four conditions; NCT06239272's 42 conditions with the histology present and the 1-30-at-biopsy criterion; the nine molecularly-defined records resolving exactly to one master protocol, seven DETERMINE arms with Arm 07 NOT_YET_RECRUITING, and one separate basket; eligibility text present for exactly three of those nine, two by per-NCT URL and the third inside the unfielded screen; the five NR4A3 term-search studies and their subjects; NCT03767075's April 2024 verification; and, most demandingly, the transport arithmetic — twelve unique lost records, five recoverable elsewhere in the same file, three of the remaining seven from the two diagnosis condition searches, with NCT00720174 COMPLETED and NCT05355753 and NCT01189253 both TERMINATED in emc-hypoxia-therapeutic-status.json. The three blockers are all one-line repairs and none touches a result: a mechanism sentence that contradicts the fetcher source the paper cites as its own fix, a false singular about how many queries ran on the one non-US registry that answered (with an omitted returned record), and a Data Availability list whose two elided filenames do not exist and which closes on three manifests when four were used. The pattern across the P2s is one thing: the paper is scrupulously bounded on the US half and looser on the non-US half, and its caveats are written almost entirely in the acceptance direction ('nothing here says any trial would accept'), while the sentences a patient could act on badly are the refusal-direction ones — 'not when it is TCF12 or TFG', 'run by a paediatric centre and enrols from age 10', 'a trial that will refuse them'. None of those is wrong at this commit; several are narrower than the record allows, and the fixes are four words each. Referee verdict: minor revision.
